title: One Gate for Every CodeYam-Only Route
description:
The component-fixture routes under /isolated-components/* now decide whether to appear by asking whether codeyam launched this server, not whether NODE_ENV says 'development'. A new predicate, codeyamLaunched in app/lib/codeyamOnly.ts, reads CODEYAM_APP_PORT — a variable the editor injects on its way to starting a dev server, so it cannot drift from what the editor actually does and is absent by construction on a server a person started themselves. The production floor those routes shared with the agent panel moved into devSurfacesPermitted in the same module, so the rule that nothing dev-only reaches production is written once; agentPanelRequested keeps its per-tab query semantics, which answer a different question. /api/codeyam-revalidate deliberately keeps its old gate, and its docstring now records why: the editor's caller reads a 404 as 'route not mounted' and proceeds with the capture anyway, so a stricter gate there would trade a harmless dev cache-flush for silently stale screenshots.

PLAN REVISION: the approved plan gated the developer escape hatch on a ?isolated=1 query param read in the layout. That is not implementable on this Next version — layouts are not passed searchParams ('Layouts do not rerender on navigation, so they cannot access search params'), and the layout is the only single place covering all 104 fixture pages, 26 of which are client components that cannot read server env at all. The user chose the env-var hatch instead: CODEYAM_APP_PORT=1 npm run dev. The plan file was updated to record the constraint and the two rejected alternatives before any code was written.

EVIDENCE: 8 new tests in app/lib/codeyamOnly.test.ts, all passing (730 registered in total). The regression case was confirmed to genuinely discriminate rather than assumed: the old NODE_ENV-only gate returns true for a hand-started dev server where the test asserts false. Captures are provably unaffected — probe-isolation-routes returned 200 on 103/103 component routes, and recapture-stale found 21 of 22 touched scenarios pixel-identical (the 22nd differs only in the capture-time origin baked into the handoff card's MCP URL by app/lib/handoffCopy.ts, a pre-existing environment sensitivity unrelated to this change). Audit passed with 0 findings; 386 scenarios fresh, 0 stale, 0 missing. README gained a section documenting that a plain npm run dev does not serve the fixture pages and how to opt in, and a stale sentence implying the agent panel always appears outside production was corrected to name ?agentPanel=1.

SCOPE VERDICT: this cycle delivered no product deliverable and deferred none — it is infrastructure hygiene on the codeyam-only route surface. All 9 product deliverables were already delivered before this cycle; the single deferred row (registering the MCP server in a client, an assist-track task) was deferred by the user in an earlier cycle and is unchanged here. No agent-decided deferrals were introduced.

KNOWN GAP, DECIDED BY THE USER: app/codeyam-isolate/layout.tsx is a third codeyam-only route surface and still carries the NODE_ENV === 'production' gate this feature exists to replace. The plan's survey counted two such routes and missed it. It was surfaced at the Present gate with an option to extend the gate to it; the user chose to save without doing so. It serves nothing today — the layout is the only file in that directory — and the glossary marks it scaffold-shipped, but a future page added under it would inherit the wrong gate, which is precisely the reintroduction path this feature was written against.
